title: Scalar extension is an exact triangulated functor
statement:
For the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], fix a prime
$\ell\neq p$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a
$\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra inclusion $E\hookrightarrow L$. Let $Y$ be any scheme.
The scalar-extension functor
$$
-\otimes_E L:D^b_c(Y,E)\longrightarrow D^b_c(Y,L)
$$
of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], obtained from the completed integral
scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] restricted by
[lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] and then rationalized, is an
exact triangulated functor: it preserves shifts and carries distinguished
triangles of $D^b_c(Y,E)$ to distinguished triangles of $D^b_c(Y,L)$.

proof.text: Use the completed coefficient sheaves, not discrete constant integral coefficients. Write $B_m=(A_{L,m})_Y$, with the ring maps $\rho_m$ and restrictions $\operatorname{Res}^L_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For any complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules, set $V(P)=\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}B_m)$ and $h_P=1-s_P$, and define $H(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(h_P)[-1]$. These termwise products exist by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus $H(P)^n=V(P)^{n-1}\oplus V(P)^n$, with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-h_Px,dx)$. On chain maps use the two diagonal product maps. Additivity, identities and composition follow componentwise from tensor and product functoriality. If $k$ is a chain homotopy between $u,v$, its product after tensoring is a degree $-1$ map $\bar k$ commuting with the transition maps; the degree $-1$ map $k_H(y,x)=(-\bar k y,\bar k x)$ is a homotopy between $H(u),H(v)$, since the off-diagonal terms cancel and the diagonal terms are $V(u-v)$. Hence $H$ descends to homotopy categories.

source.place: Agent expansion of the integral scalar-extension cone formula; homotopy differential calculation

proof.text: The shift comparison $H(P[1])\longrightarrow H(P)[1]$ is $(y,x)\mapsto(-y,x)$ and is natural. For a chain map $f:P\to Q$, termwise tensoring and products commute with the finite direct sums defining its cone. Put the four coordinates of $H(C(f))^n$ in the order $(y_Q,y_P,x_Q,x_P)$. The map $(y_Q,y_P,x_Q,x_P)\mapsto(y_Q,x_Q,-y_P,x_P)$ identifies it with $C(H(f))^n$. Indeed its differential before this permutation is $(-d_Qy_Q-fy_P-h_Qx_Q,\ d_Py_P-h_Px_P,\ d_Qx_Q+fx_P,\ -d_Px_P)$, which after the permutation is exactly the cone differential of $H(f)$. Its inverse sends $(a,b,c,d)$ to $(a,-c,b,d)$. This identification respects the cone inclusion. It also respects the connecting arrow $-p$ using the displayed shift comparison: both maps on the $P$ coordinates are $(y_P,-x_P)$. Therefore $H$ carries cone triangles to cone triangles, including the last arrow. By [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], every distinguished homotopy triangle is isomorphic to such a cone triangle, and the target localization is exact. Consequently $F=Q_LH:K(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})\to D(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y})$ is exact.

source.place: Cone differential calculation; proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated; exact derived localization

proof.text: Take as resolution class the K-flat complexes with flat terms over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. Every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from this class by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For a quasi-isomorphism between two members, clause (1) of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] says precisely that its $H$-image is a quasi-isomorphism, hence $F$ inverts it. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to the exact $F$ of step 2 and this class. Its everywhere defined left derived functor is exact and is computed by $Q_LH(P)$ on every chosen K-flat resolution. This is the functor $K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ specified in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with the same induced maps and shift comparison; the comparison on resolutions is the natural derived-functor comparison, not a choice of cones in the triangulated category.

The fixed prime satisfies $\ell\neq p$ by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], so the coefficient hypotheses of both following lemmas hold. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] this exact ambient functor maps $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ into $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_L)$. Both are full triangulated subcategories with the ambient distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated], applied for each coefficient field. Thus on these subcategories its shift comparison remains a morphism, and the image of every distinguished triangle is still distinguished. Its $\mathcal O_E$-linearity is clause (3) of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. Denote this restricted exact linear functor by $T$.

source.place: Restriction to the integral constructible subcategories; rationalization blueprint proof, integral representative clause

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the specified rational scalar-extension functor is $T_{L/E}(K)=T(K)$ and $T_{L/E}(f\otimes a)=T(f)\otimes a$, where $a\in E\subset L$. Localize the shift comparison of $T$ and its inverse. Naturality on $f\otimes a$ is the integral naturality equation tensored with $a$, and extends to sums by additivity. The two inverse equations also remain true after tensoring. This supplies a natural isomorphism $T_{L/E}(K[1])\simeq T_{L/E}(K)[1]$; its iterates give all shifts. No identification of the $\mathcal O_E$- and $\mathcal O_L$-localizations is needed.

source.place: Rational scalar extension on Hom modules, and explicit localized shift comparison

proof.text: Let $\Delta$ be distinguished in $D^b_c(Y,E)$. By [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] and [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], it is isomorphic to $Q_E(\Delta_0)$ for an integral distinguished triangle $\Delta_0$. With the shift comparison of step 5, $T_{L/E}(Q_E(\Delta_0))=Q_L(T(\Delta_0))$: all three maps, including the connecting map, are the integral images tensored with $1$. Step 4 makes $T(\Delta_0)$ distinguished and the cited localization theorem makes its $Q_L$-image distinguished. Applying $T_{L/E}$ to the triangle isomorphism gives another triangle isomorphism. Hence $T_{L/E}(\Delta)$ is distinguished. Together with step 5 this proves both clauses of the item.
